candidates.subject: The Hyde Park House, Paul Cornell's four-story lakefront resort hotel at 53rd Street and Lake Michigan, the social center of early Hyde Park (built 1857, where Mary Todd Lincoln stayed in 1865).
candidates.commonsSearch: Hyde Park House Chicago 53rd Street hotel
candidates.beat: Cornell builds the Hyde Park House and markets the township as a lakeside resort suburb; bridges directly to the Mary Todd Lincoln beat, since she lodged here in 1865.

candidates.subject: The Illinois Central Railroad's Great Central Station train shed in Chicago, an 1856 engraving from Frank Leslie's Illustrated Newspaper showing the IC's first permanent Chicago depot.
candidates.commonsSearch: Great Central Station trainshed Illinois Central 1856
candidates.beat: The Illinois Central commuter line is what makes Cornell's suburb possible; this shows the railroad's grand new Chicago terminal the year before Hyde Park's first depot.

candidates.subject: Lincoln's funeral car on the old Illinois Central Railroad tracks on the trestle over Lake Michigan, Chicago, photographed by F. E. Stebbins in 1865.
candidates.commonsSearch: Lincoln funeral car Illinois Central railroad Lake Michigan Chicago 1865
candidates.beat: Shows the actual Illinois Central lakefront trestle in 1865 and links to the Mary Todd Lincoln / Lincoln-mourning thread; the same IC line carried Hyde Park's commuters.

candidates.subject: Map of Cook County, Illinois (W. L. Flower, engraved by Edward Mendel, 1861), which includes a plat inset of Hyde Park, the year Hyde Park Township was incorporated.
candidates.commonsSearch: Map of Cook County Illinois 1861 Mendel Flower
candidates.beat: Hyde Park Township is incorporated in 1861; an authentic period plat shows the township's place in early Cook County. Library of Congress item 2013593074 is the public-domain source if not already on Commons.

candidates.subject: South front of the Great Central railway station, just completed at Chicago, Illinois, a contemporary 1856 illustration of the Illinois Central's lakefront depot exterior.

candidates.subject: George R. Lawrence kite/balloon bird's-eye aerial panorama of the early University of Chicago campus and the Midway Plaisance, circa 1904-1907. Shows the Gothic quadrangles, surrounding Hyde Park, and the open Midway in one sweeping view; covers the requested Midway-with-campus image. Original LOC panoramic negative LOT 5785 no. 36, loc.gov/item/2007663921; LOC panoramic scans are very large. Confirm Commons availability; if absent, source from loc.gov.
candidates.commonsSearch: University of Chicago bird's eye view Lawrence panorama
candidates.beat: Opening establishing shot of the chapter, over Rockefeller's money building a campus from nothing and Cobb laying out the gray Gothic quads.
